questions.q: Why does this lesson treat presenting the work as part of the actual work?
options: A pipeline nobody can explain is a pipeline nobody else can safely maintain
Presentations are only relevant for management roles, not engineers
Technical work speaks for itself and never needs explanation
It's purely a formality with no real professional value
questions.explain: In a real job, a clear walkthrough is often the actual deliverable a reviewer relies on, since almost nobody has time to read every activity's configuration themselves.

questions.q: In the five-minute walkthrough structure, what comes after describing the architecture at a glance?
options: One deliberate design decision, explained with its real reasoning
A complete line-by-line reading of every activity's JSON
Immediately moving to unrelated future project ideas
Nothing — the architecture overview is the entire walkthrough
questions.explain: After the architecture overview, the structure calls for picking one genuinely interesting design decision (like the Filter-before-Join ordering) rather than listing every choice made.

questions.q: What does the walkthrough's requirement callback table actually demonstrate?
options: Proof, not just assertion, that the finished pipeline satisfies each of Lesson 53's original requirements
A list of features that were considered but never built
An unrelated summary of Azure pricing
A ranking of which chapters were hardest to complete
questions.explain: Mapping each original stakeholder requirement to the specific lesson/feature that satisfies it closes the walkthrough with concrete proof rather than a vague claim of completeness.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend keeping from the capstone as a portfolio artifact?
options: A short README with the business problem and design decisions, plus the actual pipeline/data flow JSON
Nothing — capstone work should be deleted once the course ends
Only a screenshot of the final "Succeeded" status
A video recording with no written documentation
questions.explain: A written README plus the concrete JSON definitions turns the capstone into real, presentable evidence of applied skill, not just a completed course checklist.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what marks genuine completion of the course?
options: Being able to deliver the five-minute walkthrough out loud from memory, not reading it off the screen
Simply reaching the final page of the course content
Passing a multiple-choice quiz with a perfect score
Having every pipeline JSON file saved somewhere
questions.explain: The lesson's actual bar for finishing is being able to explain the finished work clearly and confidently, from memory — genuine understanding, not just having clicked through every lesson.
